content:
Marta: :rotating_light: ap-se1 rack-42 provisioning failures after last BMC push. Nodes are toggling UEFI secure-boot during PXE -> UEFI handoff and serial consoles drop. ~12/48 GPU hosts not coming up, scheduler queues spiking. Rolling back a test host fixed it. Paging oncall and firmware folks. infra-bot, paste the logs?

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-0023. Collected logs from rack-42 provisioner and BMC interfaces. Link: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-2026-0423-0023

Anj: which fw image was pushed? saw a batch labelled bmc-fw-2026-03-18-v5.2 overnight. Also noticed SFP negotiation flapping on eth0 for a few nodes — that could interrupt PXE traffic.

Marta: here's a short snippet from the serial console and ipmitool output for node03:
```
[  102.345678] watchdog: hardware watchdog triggered reset
IPMI: Chassis power cycle requested by mgmt-console
UEFI: SecureBoot state change detected -> enabled
DHCP: no offer (PXE timeout)
```

Kyle: if rollback on one host worked can we roll the rack back to v5.1 while investigating? we need to weigh tenant compliance vs availability. Also need to check reserved-capacity customers that might be impacted.

Selena: we can't flip secure-boot policy globally (compliance). Mitigation options: 1) staged rollback of rack-42 BMC image, 2) divert non-prod provisioning to eu-fallback region until fix, 3) targeted power-cycles. Note cost hit for cross-region provisioning: approx ~$2.5k/day if we push GPUs cross-region. cc @Marc (oncall) :thinking_face:

Marc (oncall): oncall here. Start a canary rollback for rack-42 now, soak 30m. If stable, rollback remaining affected racks sequentially. I'll open the customer impact notice. Who can trigger the rollback?

Anj: I can. running: `ipmi-fw rollback --host rack42-node03 --image bmc-v5.1`
Anj: exit 0 on node03, issuing soft-reboot now. watching serial console.

infra-bot: rack42-node03 -> PROVISIONED at 2612345705. Log excerpt: "UEFI boot success, secureboot state retained and stable" :white_check_mark:

Marta: after ~20m node03 fully recovered and joined cluster. Proceeding with staged rollback for remaining affected nodes. Need a postmortem: why did v5.2 flip SFP negotiation and toggle UEFI attr? assign to eng-firmware + eng-provisioner.

Kyle: add an Optimize/Autoscale ticket to avoid SLA slips when a rack-level provisioning blast occurs (lower impact by temporary capacity buffer). :thumbsup:

Selena: I'll draft the customer note + short cost impact summary and tag support. Incident labels: provisioning, bmc-fw, region-ap-se1, mitigation-rollback, followup-fw-repro, prov-policy-hardening.
